entries.note: The comparison supplies no shared criterion for how similar the two men are.

entries.test: Public studies and documented incidents showing the prevalence and severity of harms from excessive reliance on AI would test this claim.
entries.note: In context, this asserts a substantial practical problem supported by examples of professional failures.
The extension from law and journalism to warfare is explicitly qualified as likely.

entries.test: Public evaluations and incident investigations would show whether human oversight can leave consequential AI errors undetected, especially when outputs appear plausible.
entries.note: The context supports a claim that human oversight does not guarantee safety. Saying it does not reliably prevent errors is stronger.
Marcus endorses the possibility in his own voice, without asserting that Claude selected the school.

entries.test: Public investigations of targeting operations with overloaded operators who overtrust AI would establish whether serious targeting errors occur under those conditions.
entries.note: The prediction is categorical but gives no deadline.
The normalization omits the possibility of renewed military involvement and drops the qualification that human involvement is putative. Responsibility for deaths is explicitly only a possibility.

entries.test: Public statements, promised timelines, subsequent revisions, and responses to missed promises would test the alleged recurring pattern for Amodei and Altman.
entries.note: The normalization removes the qualification 'pretty much' and omits the stated frequency of deadline changes.

entries.test: Dated public statements from both men would show whether they repeatedly forecast imminent AGI and subsequently postponed those timelines after non-delivery.
entries.note: The rhetorical 'endlessly' has a plain reading as repeated behavior.

entries.test: The August 2023 podcast, contemporaneous definitions of AGI, and publicly demonstrated capabilities by August 2026 would test the prediction Marcus rejects.
entries.note: Marcus disputes the plausibility of arrival within the predicted window; the normalization substitutes a statement about non-arrival. The full three-year window had not expired when he wrote.

entries.test: Public demographic and clinical evidence by March 8, 2036 would show whether human lifespan has doubled relative to the publication baseline.
entries.note: 'Zero chance' expresses a categorical negative prediction here. The preceding discussion supplies the clinical-testing rationale.

entries.test: Public comparative evaluations of AI and Nobel-caliber scientists across most science and engineering fields would test whether AI achieves the superiority Marcus rejects.
entries.note: The supplied text gives no deadline for this prediction; January 2025 dates the op-ed.
This is a denunciation rather than a specific factual allegation of knowing deception.

entries.test: Public fundraising pitches and statements would show whether Altman and Amodei repeatedly invoke catastrophic AI risks while soliciting investment to accelerate development.
entries.note: The paraphrase is Marcus's own characterization. Its observable fundraising pattern can be tested without establishing private motives.

entries.test: Anthropic's original safety pledge and its late-February 2026 policy changes would show whether it abandoned the core commitment.
entries.note: The publication date supports resolving 'late February' to 2026.
'Speedrunning' a 'fall from grace' is a rhetorical assessment without a defined outcome.

The normalization drops 'often' and 'largely.' The overall characterization of a principal job as fundraising through hype has no shared test, although costs and profitability are separately checkable.

entries.test: Public training-data disclosures, court records, and dataset documentation would show whether OpenAI broadly used publicly accessible material regardless of copyright status.
entries.note: 'Practically anything' plainly alleges broad inclusion, rather than a literal inventory of every public item.

The normalization narrows 'same thing' from broad use of publicly available material to some copyrighted material. Its ethical judgment cannot be settled by evidence, although use of Marcus's books can.

entries.test: Public operating-cost measurements, task-success evaluations, security studies, and Anthropic's commercial agent offerings would test these claims about agents.
entries.note: These are practical assertions about costs, reliability, security, and commercial benefit.

entries.test: Dated product launches, demonstrations, and promotion by Anthropic and its competitors would show whether Anthropic was an early leading promoter of computer-control agents.
entries.note: 'At the forefront' has a plain reading as early, prominent involvement.

The normalization drops the comparison with almost everyone Marcus can think of and broadens the exceptions beyond mass surveillance and fully autonomous weapons. The overall personal resemblance has no shared evidentiary test.
